title: Introduction to Docker & Containerization
description: Deployment evolution, virtual machines, containers, and Docker architecture.
objectives: Explain dual booting, virtualization, and containerization
Identify Docker client, daemon, images, registry, and containers

sections.title: Deployment evolution
sections.body: Dual booting allows multiple operating systems on one machine but generally requires a reboot to switch. Virtual machines run guest operating systems through a hypervisor, typically with their own kernels. Containers isolate processes while sharing the host operating-system kernel, reducing overhead and usually improving startup speed.

sections.title: Docker architecture
sections.body: The Docker client sends API requests to the Docker daemon. The daemon manages images, containers, networks, and volumes. Registries such as Docker Hub distribute images. An image is a read-only template; a container is a runnable instance with a writable layer.

sections.title: Containers vs virtual machines
sections.body: Virtual machines provide guest OS isolation and are suitable when different kernels are required. Containers are generally lighter and more portable between compatible systems, but they share the host kernel.

quiz: The Docker daemon manages Docker objects.
Which statement is true about containers?
Each container requires a separate kernel
They share the host OS kernel
Ordinary Linux containers share the host Linux kernel.
Images are templates used to create containers.
Where can images be downloaded from?
Docker Hub is a popular image registry.
interview: What is containerization?
Packaging an application and its dependencies in an isolated environment that shares the host OS kernel.
How do containers differ from VMs?
VMs typically run separate guest kernels; containers share the host kernel and isolate processes.
What does the Docker daemon do?
It manages Docker images, containers, networks, and volumes through an API.
What is Docker Hub?
A hosted registry for distributing container images.
Why do containers start quickly?
They start processes without booting a separate guest operating system.

Create a comparison table for kernel, startup time, resource overhead, and isolation.
Explore Docker Engine
Run docker version and docker info; identify client and server details.
Run your first container
Pull nginx, start it, list it, stop it, and remove it.

title: Docker Installation & Container Lifecycle
description: Install Docker on Ubuntu, manage permissions, and operate container states.
objectives: Install and verify Docker on Ubuntu
Create, attach, detach, stop, restart, and remove containers

sections.title: Install Docker on Ubuntu
sections.body: On a disposable Ubuntu cloud VM, update package indexes, install docker.io, and start the Docker service. Verify the client and daemon. Docker group membership grants effectively root-level control and should be limited to trusted users.

sections.title: Interactive versus detached containers
sections.body: The -i flag keeps standard input open, -t allocates a pseudo-terminal, and -d starts a container detached. These flags are not required for every container. Containers stop when their main process exits.

sections.title: Lifecycle and cleanup
sections.body: docker run creates and starts a container; docker start restarts an existing stopped container. Ctrl+P followed by Ctrl+Q detaches from an attached container. docker exec starts an additional process inside a running container. docker system prune -a can remove stopped containers, unused networks, unused images, and build cache; review before confirming.

quiz: Which command installs Docker from Ubuntu repositories?
Ubuntu packages Docker Engine as docker.io.
-i and -t are useful for interactive shells.
docker start operates on an existing container.
Which shortcut detaches without stopping the main process?
Docker uses Ctrl+P then Ctrl+Q by default.
interview: docker run vs docker start?
run creates and starts a new container; start runs an existing stopped container.
docker attach vs docker exec?
attach connects to the main process streams; exec launches a new process.
Why does an interactive Ubuntu container exit?
Its main shell exits, so the container main process ends.
How do you resolve Docker socket permission errors?
Check daemon status, socket access, group membership, and refresh the login session.
What is the risk of docker group membership?
It effectively provides root-level control of the Docker host.
assignments: Install Docker
Install Docker on Ubuntu and capture docker version and service status.
Practice lifecycle
Run an interactive Ubuntu container, detach, attach, exit, and restart it.
Clean up safely
Remove stopped lab containers and inspect disk usage using docker system df.

title: Application Containers & Custom Images
description: Run Apache, publish ports, customize a website, commit, tag, and push images.
objectives: Create and share a customized image

sections.title: Run Apache HTTP Server
sections.body: The official Apache HTTP Server image is httpd:2.4. docker run -d starts it detached. Publishing -p 7070:80 routes host port 7070 to container port 80. Detached containers still produce logs viewable with docker logs.

sections.title: Customize the site
sections.body: Use docker exec to start a shell or command in a running container. For the official httpd image, the document root is /usr/local/apache2/htdocs. Container filesystem changes are ephemeral when the container is removed unless captured in an image or stored persistently.

sections.title: Commit and publish
sections.body: docker commit creates an image from a container’s writable filesystem changes (not mounted volumes). Tag it with your Docker Hub namespace, authenticate using a personal access token, and push. For reproducible production images, prefer Dockerfiles over manual commits.

commands:
docker exec myapache sh -c 'echo "

My Docker Website

" > /usr/local/apache2/htdocs/index.html'
quiz: What is the official Apache HTTP Server image?
commit captures writable container filesystem changes in an image.
How do you view detached container logs?
What is preferable for reproducible image builds?
Dockerfiles make builds repeatable and reviewable.
interview: Explain -d versus -it.
-d detaches the container; -it provides interactive input and a pseudo-terminal.
What is port publishing?
Mapping a host IP/port to a container port to make the service reachable through the host.
docker exec vs docker attach?
exec starts a new process; attach connects to the main process.
Why use docker tag before pushing?
The image must be named for the target registry repository, typically username/repository:tag.
Why prefer Dockerfiles to docker commit?
Dockerfiles document reproducible, version-controlled image builds.
assignments: Deploy Apache
Run httpd:2.4 on host port 7070 and capture the page and docker ps output.
Customize and commit
Replace index.html, commit to mywebsite:v1, and test the result.
Publish to Docker Hub
Tag, push, and redeploy your image; submit the repository URL.

title: MySQL & WordPress Multi-Container Architecture
description: Deploy a database, execute SQL, connect WordPress, and troubleshoot service dependencies.
objectives: Run a MySQL database container and execute SQL
Connect WordPress and MySQL over a user-defined bridge network

sections.title: Database containers
sections.body: MySQL can run as a container initialized with a root password, application database, and application user. Connect through docker exec and the mysql CLI. Database ports do not need to be published to the host when another container accesses MySQL on the same Docker network.

sections.title: WordPress multi-container architecture
sections.body: WordPress is a CMS that uses a database for posts, users, and settings. Deploy WordPress and MySQL as separate containers on a user-defined bridge network. Configure WORDPRESS_DB_HOST with the MySQL container name, not a hardcoded IP address.

sections.title: Networking, resilience, and security
sections.body: A database outage disrupts database-dependent WordPress operations. A user-defined bridge provides name resolution and scoped connectivity. Keep database ports private, use least-privilege credentials, and store MySQL data in a persistent volume. Network separation is not a replacement for authentication.

commands: docker run -d --name mysql-db --network wp-network -e MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD=RootLab123 -e MYSQL_DATABASE=wordpressdb -e MYSQL_USER=wpuser -e MYSQL_PASSWORD=WpLab123 -v mysql-data:/var/lib/mysql mysql:8.4

docker run -d --name wordpress-app --network wp-network -p 8080:80 -e WORDPRESS_DB_HOST=mysql-db:3306 -e WORDPRESS_DB_USER=wpuser -e WORDPRESS_DB_PASSWORD=WpLab123 -e WORDPRESS_DB_NAME=wordpressdb -v wordpress-data:/var/www/html wordpress:php8.3-apache
quiz: Which variable sets the MySQL root password?
The official MySQL image supports MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD.
How should WordPress locate MySQL on a user-defined bridge?
User-defined bridges support container-name DNS resolution.
Does MySQL port 3306 need to be published to the host for WordPress on the same network?
Containers on the same network can communicate directly.
Why use a volume for MySQL?
Volumes retain data independently of container replacement.
What happens when MySQL is unavailable?
WordPress relies on its database for normal operation.
interview: What is multi-container architecture?
Separate application components run in distinct containers and communicate over a network.
Why separate WordPress and MySQL?
They can be configured, updated, and managed independently.
Why use container names instead of IP addresses?
Container IP addresses may change when containers are recreated.
How do you troubleshoot database connection errors?
Check container status, logs, network, credentials, readiness, and database privileges.
How do you protect a containerized database?
Avoid unnecessary published ports, use isolated networks, least-privilege accounts, secrets, volumes, and backups.
assignments: Create a MySQL database
Run MySQL, create a table, insert five rows, and filter with WHERE.
Deploy WordPress
Connect WordPress and MySQL over wp-network and complete setup.
Simulate failure
